context: Tests recommendation with options, the layered structure, concise writing and not assuming technical knowledge.

checklist.name: Audience stated
checklist.description: The response states the audience as an executive or director with no technical background before the briefing.

checklist.name: Recommendation named
checklist.description: The briefing states which of options A, B or C is recommended.

checklist.name: Recommendation in the opening
checklist.description: The opening paragraph contains the problem, the business impact and the recommended action.

checklist.name: Options not left unranked
checklist.description: The briefing does not present A, B and C neutrally without saying which is preferred.

checklist.name: Owner and deadline for the decision
checklist.description: The required action follows `[Owner] must [action] by [deadline]` with a named owner and a concrete date.

checklist.name: No unexplained jargon
checklist.description: Terms such as failover, replication lag and query plan are translated or removed in the main text.

checklist.name: Technical detail moved to an appendix
checklist.description: The failover times, replication lag figures and query plan analysis appear only in a clearly separated appendix or are omitted from the main text.

checklist.name: Main text is short and scannable
checklist.description: The main body has short paragraphs or a short list rather than long blocks of text.

checklist.name: Nothing assumed about prior knowledge
checklist.description: Where a technical idea is needed, it is explained in everyday terms rather than assumed to be known.

checklist.name: Costs and effort shown in business terms
checklist.description: The 18k a year cost and the six-month, two-engineer effort are shown as business impact.
